about.title: About Unix Timestamp Converter - Epoch Date Time Tool
about.description: The Unix Timestamp Converter specializes in converting Unix timestamps to human-readable dates and vice versa. Essential for developers working with Unix systems, databases, and APIs that store time as epoch values. Provides precise conversion with support for both 32-bit and 64-bit timestamps, handling the full range from 1970 to beyond 2038, making it future-proof for modern applications and development workflows.

faq.q: What is the Unix epoch and how does it work?
faq.a: The Unix epoch is January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. Unix timestamps count seconds (or milliseconds) from this point in time. This standardized reference point allows consistent time representation across different systems and programming languages.

The 2038 problem affects 32-bit systems where timestamps overflow. However, modern 64-bit systems and this converter support timestamps well beyond 2038, extending usability for centuries into the future.
Yes, negative timestamps represent dates before January 1, 1970, and are fully supported for historical date conversions. This allows working with dates from any point in history.

faq.q: How precise are the timestamp conversions?
faq.a: Conversions are precise to the second for standard Unix timestamps. Millisecond precision is available for extended formats, ensuring accuracy for high-precision timing applications and database operations.
